bullets: ‘Marley was dead: to begin with.’; ‘Old Marley was as dead as a door-nail.’ The narrator then jokes that he doesn’t know what is especially dead about a door-nail: **humour** and intimacy.
‘as close to it as I am now to you, and I am standing in the spirit at your elbow’ (Stave 2): **direct address**; the narrator and reader stand together.
The narrator comments: ‘I should have liked… to have been a member of it’ (Belle’s family): personal feeling guides the reader’s emotions.
core.p: The narrator is a first-person storyteller who speaks to the reader as if sitting beside them.

bullets: Scrooge’s ‘There’s more of gravy than of grave about you’ to Marley: a pun; Scrooge uses humour to hide fear.
Exaggerated descriptions (Fezziwig’s calves ‘shone in every part of the dance like moons’).
The Cratchits’ pudding ‘like a speckled cannon-ball’: comic warmth.
Humour makes the moral message enjoyable and keeps the ghost story from becoming too dark.
The narrator judges Scrooge (‘old sinner!’) and praises the generous.
He invites the reader to sympathise with the poor and question their own attitudes.
The Preface: ‘May it haunt their houses pleasantly’: the narrator speaks to the reader’s home and conscience.

callouts.p: Dickens’s warm, humorous, intrusive narrator acts like a friend telling a story by the fire, so his social criticism feels like a shared moral conversation rather than a lecture.

model: Context: reading aloud, Dickens’s public readings, purpose
exam.q: Explain how Dickens uses the narrator to influence the reader. (20 marks)
exam.tip: Link the narrator’s voice to Dickens’s purpose every time.

mistakes.r: The narrator is a separate storyteller voice.

quotes.q: standing in the spirit at your elbow
more of gravy than of grave

quotes.a: Comic, affectionate description of the pudding.

summary: Dickens’s narrator is an intrusive, humorous, conversational voice that addresses the reader directly, jokes, comments on characters and guides the reader’s moral response, making the ghost story warm and persuasive.

terms.d: A narrator who comments on events and addresses the reader.
A joke using a word’s double meaning or similar sound.
